Piotr Karcz Appointed Chief Executive at Polskie Sieci Gazowo-Wodne

Polskie Sieci Gazowo-Wodne (PSGW), one of Poland’s leading gas and water utilities providers, announced on Tuesday the appointment of Piotr Karcz as its new Chief Executive Officer, effective July 1st. Karcz, 52, brings more than two decades of industry experience, having previously held senior leadership roles at multiple energy and infrastructure firms across Central Europe.

The decision was confirmed following a meeting of the PSGW Supervisory Board in Warsaw. Outgoing CEO, Marta Kubicka, will remain with the company in an advisory capacity until September to ensure a smooth transition.

“We are delighted to welcome Mr. Karcz to the PSGW leadership team,” said Supervisory Board Chairman Andrzej Malinowski. “His deep sector knowledge and proven track record in managing complex infrastructure projects make him well-suited to lead the company as we continue to modernise Poland’s gas and water networks.”

Karcz is expected to oversee several major projects, including the expansion of the national water grid in the Mazowieckie and Śląskie regions, and ongoing investments to upgrade gas distribution systems in line with new EU regulations on emissions and safety.

“PSGW plays a vital role in ensuring reliable gas and water supplies to millions of Polish households,” Karcz said in a statement. “I look forward to working with our talented employees and partners to deliver on our commitments to customers, communities, and the environment.”

Industry analysts welcomed the appointment, citing Karcz’s reputation for innovation and consensus-building. “Piotr Karcz is known for his pragmatic approach and ability to foster collaboration among stakeholders,” said Beata Nowicka, energy sector analyst at the Warsaw Institute for Infrastructure. “His leadership comes at a time when the utilities sector faces both challenges and opportunities arising from the energy transition and water management reforms.”

Union representatives also expressed optimism. “We value management that engages with workers and understands the realities in the field,” commented Zbigniew Kulesza, spokesperson for the Utilities Workers’ Union.

PSGW supplies gas and water to over 5 million customers nationwide and employs more than 4,000 staff. The company has stated its strategic focus will remain on reliability, safety, and sustainable development under Karcz’s leadership.
